regime: Quiet holiday pause after Wednesday's whipsaw: metals steady, oil holding its jump
takeaway: With US markets shut for Thanksgiving, gold slipped about 0.7% to near $3,564 in thin trading while silver rose about 1%, pulling the gold/silver ratio down to about 86, which eases the silver-under-stress check a little. Brent held near $95 after Wednesday's 3.5% jump on the Houthi refinery claim, so the oil-shock check stays in view, while the yen and the dollar barely moved, so there is no sign of a carry unwind. Stock funds, yields and the VIX still show Wednesday's closes until trading resumes Friday.
